newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SMITH CRITICISES FRENCH ATTITUDE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMITH CRITICISES FRENCH ATTITUDE.

text.p: Australia coach Greg Smith on Friday described France as their own worst enemy and criticised the Five Nations champions' poor discipline.
Speaking on the eve of Saturday's second and final test, Smith said France stood a better chance of levelling the series at Ballymore if they abandoned their spoiling tactics.
Smith castigated France for creating "outright chaos" by repeatedly ignoring the laws of the game in tour matches in their attempts to spoil the opposition's possession.
"I don't think all these stoppages are helping the French -- they are hindering them," Smith said.
Australia won the first test 29-15 last weekend but the game failed to live up to expectations because of the large number of stoppages.
The French were repeatedly penalised for killing the ball and persistent off-side at the breakdown.
Smith said the French were ruining their own chances and failing to exploit their strength in running the ball in the backs by giving away so many penalties.
"I imagined the games against France were going to be really fast, spectacular games and that's what I would like to see," said Smith.
France assistant coach Pierre Villepreux has been unhappy with the refereeing on tour, saying his players were mystified by the number of penalties awarded against them.
The tourists have argued that they adopted exactly the same approach during the Five Nations tournament without penalty.
French selectors made three changes for the second test, recalling goalkicking centre Christophe Lamaison and fly-half Alain Penaud after injury while promoting winger Sebastien Viars.
Centre Richard Dourthe, fly-half David Aucagne and winger David Venditti were all relegated to the bench.
Australia's preparations were disrupted when injuries ruled out full-back Matt Burke and number eight Daniel Manu. They were replaced by Stephen Larkham and veteran back-rower Troy Coker.
Burke's absence with a recurrence of a groin injury cleared a space on the bench for winger Mitch Hardy, the surprise hero for the Wallabies in the first test.
Hardy scored two quick tries to secure the victory during a brief stint as a temporarty replacement while Larkham left the field for treatment to a facial injury.

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Troy Coker, 7-David Wilson, 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-David Giffin, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.
